title: Join 3 clips back to back: still the same character? Swap the music: does the picture change too?
summary: Use the last frame of one clip as the first frame of the next. After 3 clips, the character never changed. And changing just the one music line swaps the background music with zero picture change - even writing nothing about music still gets you a soundtrack.

stats: Two tests: 1) use the last frame of each shot as the first frame of the next, chained for 3 shots in a row; 2) keep one picture and pair it with 4 different music instructions, one version each
No face swap across 3 shots: twin tails, sailor uniform, gold buttons, headphones and face shape stay stable throughout, no face swap and no outfit change
Prompt unchanged, seed (the random number used for generation, same value or the results aren't comparable) unchanged, only the first-frame source or the one music line changed
Does changing music change the picture?
No: characters, stage and camera are identical across the 4 versions; and the 4 audio tracks all differ from each other, so the music line really does control the genre
After 3 shots the face skews slightly younger; keep it to 3-4 shots or correct with a reference image now and then. Also, writing no music instruction still gets you a soundtrack
findings: Using the last frame of a clip as the first frame of the next naturally reads as the 'next shot' camera logic, so transitions stay seamless; for a hard-cut feel, reuse the same reference image with a different seed (the random number, i.e. a new generation starting point)
The music line can be edited on its own: to swap the background music, just change that line, no need to re-roll the picture
No music written does not mean no sound: H3 auto-adds a soundtrack even without a music instruction, so for a quiet scene you must spell it out in the prompt
